subject: ela
verification_note: cde.ca.gov blocks automated fetches (web-firewall redirect), so these topics were written from knowledge of the California standards and NOT checked against the page; the listed sources are where to verify them. Review in a browser before relying on it.
note: California ELA/Literacy (CA CCSS) and ELD skills by grade, summarized in my own words. cde.ca.gov blocked automated page fetches (web application firewall redirect), so the URLs were NOT read in this session and skills come from prior knowledge of the standards and framework strands; no standard codes are given. CDE does not publish an official spelling or vocabulary list, so word lists are representative grade-appropriate examples that match the framework's skills.

items.subject: ela
items.title: Letter names and sounds
items.summary: Every letter has a name and a sound. Say the letter, then say the sound it makes, like /b/ for b.

items.subject: ela
items.title: Rhyming words
items.summary: Words that rhyme end with the same sound, like cat and hat. Can you think of a word that rhymes with dog?

items.subject: ela
items.title: Clapping syllables
items.summary: Words have beats called syllables. Clap as you say them: ap-ple has two claps, and ba-na-na has three.

items.subject: ela
items.title: Blending sounds into words
items.summary: Say each sound slowly and then slide them together: /c/ /a/ /t/ makes cat. That is how you read a new word.

items.subject: ela
items.title: How books work
items.summary: You read a book from front to back, and words go left to right and top to bottom. Spaces show where one word ends.

items.subject: ela
items.title: Retelling a story
items.summary: After you hear a story, tell what happened using the characters, the setting, and the big events.

items.subject: ela
items.title: Asking questions about a book
items.summary: Good readers ask who, what, where, and why. You can ask a question about a story or a true book you hear.

items.subject: ela
items.title: Drawing, dictating, and writing
items.summary: You can share ideas by drawing and then telling or writing about your picture. Try writing the sounds you hear.

items.subject: ela
items.title: Capital letters and your name
items.summary: Names start with a capital letter. Sentences start with a capital letter too. Practice writing your own name.

items.subject: ela
items.title: Taking turns to talk
items.summary: In a conversation we listen to the speaker, wait for our turn, and then share our own idea.

items.subject: ela
items.title: Learning English words
items.summary: If you speak another language at home, that is a strength! You can learn English words by pointing, listening, and saying them aloud.

items.subject: ela
items.title: Short a words
items.summary: Listen for the short a sound, like in cat. Sound out each word and write it.

items.subject: ela
items.title: Short i words
items.summary: Short i sounds like the middle of sit. Stretch out the sounds to spell these.

items.subject: ela
items.title: Short o words
items.summary: Short o sounds like the middle of dog. Say each sound and write it down.

items.subject: ela
items.title: Everyday sight words
items.summary: Some words are used all the time, so we learn them by sight. Try to read these without sounding them out.

items.subject: ela
items.title: Opposites and position words
items.summary: Words like up and down, in and out, big and little tell where things are or how they are different.

items.subject: ela
items.title: Digraphs: sh, ch, th, wh
items.summary: Two letters can team up to make one sound, like sh in ship or ch in chip.

items.subject: ela
items.title: Silent e makes vowels say their name
items.summary: A silent e at the end can make the vowel say its name: cap becomes cape, and kit becomes kite.

items.subject: ela
items.title: Word endings -s, -ed, -ing
items.summary: Endings change a word. Jump, jumps, jumped, and jumping tell about one or many, now or before.

items.subject: ela
items.title: Syllables in words
items.summary: Every syllable has a vowel sound. Count the beats to read longer words like rab-bit and pic-nic.

items.subject: ela
items.title: Characters, setting, and events
items.summary: Stories have characters, a setting where they happen, and events in order. Tell the key details when you retell.

items.subject: ela
items.title: Text features in true books
items.summary: Headings, pictures, captions, and glossaries help you find facts fast in a nonfiction book.

items.subject: ela
items.title: Opinion, informing, and storytelling
items.summary: First graders write opinions with a reason, facts about a topic, and short stories with a beginning, middle, and end.

items.subject: ela
items.title: Sentences and punctuation
items.summary: A sentence starts with a capital letter and ends with a period, question mark, or exclamation point.

items.subject: ela
items.title: Speaking in complete sentences
items.summary: Listen carefully, ask a question if you do not understand, and answer in a whole sentence.

items.subject: ela
items.title: Using English to share ideas
items.summary: English learners can build sentences by adding details: I see a dog, then I see a big brown dog.

items.subject: ela
items.title: Silent e words
items.summary: These words have a long vowel and a silent e at the end.

items.subject: ela
items.title: Digraph words
items.summary: Each word has sh, ch, th, or wh. Listen for the special sound.

items.subject: ela
items.title: Blend words
items.summary: Blends keep both letter sounds, like st in stop and fl in flag.

items.subject: ela
items.title: Sight words that matter
items.summary: These tricky words do not always sound the way they look. Learn them by heart.

items.subject: ela
items.title: Feeling words
items.summary: Words like happy, sad, and proud tell how people feel. Use them to talk about characters in stories.

items.subject: ela
items.title: Opposites
items.summary: Opposites are words with meanings that are very different, like hot and cold.

items.subject: ela
items.title: Long vowel teams
items.summary: Two vowels can work together, like ai in rain, oa in boat, and ee in seed. The first one often says its name.

items.subject: ela
items.title: R-controlled vowels
items.summary: When r follows a vowel it changes the sound, like in car, bird, and corn.

items.subject: ela
items.title: Prefixes and suffixes
items.summary: Add un- or re- to the start of a word, or -ful or -less to the end, and the meaning changes: careful, careless.

items.subject: ela
items.title: Who, what, where, when, why, how
items.summary: Ask these questions to show you understand a story. Look back in the book to find your answers.

items.subject: ela
items.title: Stories with a lesson
items.summary: Many stories, like fables, teach a lesson or message. Tell what the characters learned.

items.subject: ela
items.title: Main topic of a text
items.summary: The main topic is what a whole passage is mostly about. Details give the facts that support it.

items.subject: ela
items.title: Opinion, informative, and narrative writing
items.summary: Second graders write opinions with reasons, facts about a topic, and stories with feelings and a clear ending.

items.subject: ela
items.title: Nouns, verbs, and adjectives
items.summary: Nouns name things, verbs show action, and adjectives describe. In The red ball bounced, ball is a noun.

items.subject: ela
items.title: Irregular plurals and contractions
items.summary: One mouse, two mice! Some plurals change completely. A contraction squeezes two words together: do not becomes don't.

items.subject: ela
items.title: Sharing in a group
items.summary: Take turns, build on what others say, and speak clearly when you tell a story or share facts.

items.subject: ela
items.title: English learners and storytelling
items.summary: Practice telling what happened first, next, and last. Use new English words from books in your own sentences.

items.subject: ela
items.title: Vowel team words
items.summary: These long vowel sounds are spelled with two or more letters.

items.subject: ela
items.title: R-controlled words
items.summary: The r changes the vowel sound in these words.

items.subject: ela
items.title: Diphthong words
items.summary: Sounds like ow in cloud and oy in toy glide from one sound to another.

items.subject: ela
items.title: Contractions
items.summary: An apostrophe shows where letters were left out.

items.subject: ela
items.title: Story words
items.summary: These words show up in many stories. Can you use one in a sentence?

items.subject: ela
items.title: Words for a nonfiction book
items.summary: Learn the words that help you read true books about animals and nature.

items.subject: ela
items.title: Reading long words by parts
items.summary: Break long words into prefixes, roots, and endings to read them: un-happi-ness. Practice until reading flows smoothly.

items.subject: ela
items.title: Asking and answering questions about a text
items.summary: Ask questions while you read, then point to the exact words and pictures in the text that answer them.

items.subject: ela
items.title: Central message and character traits
items.summary: A central message is the big lesson of a story. Characters' actions and words show what they are like.

items.subject: ela
items.title: Point of view
items.summary: Who is telling the story? Your point of view can be different from the narrator's or a character's.

items.subject: ela
items.title: Text features and main idea
items.summary: Use headings, maps, and diagrams to find the main idea and key details of a nonfiction text.

items.subject: ela
items.title: Opinion writing
items.summary: State your opinion, give reasons, link them with words like because and also, and end with a closing sentence.

items.subject: ela
items.title: Informative and narrative writing
items.summary: Introduce a topic and group related facts. For stories, use dialogue and describe what characters think and feel.

items.subject: ela
items.title: Planning, revising, and editing
items.summary: Good writers plan first, then revise with a friend or teacher, and finally check spelling and punctuation.

items.subject: ela
items.title: Parts of speech and verb tenses
items.summary: Nouns, pronouns, verbs, adjectives, and adverbs have jobs. Verbs show past, present, or future: walked, walk, will walk.

items.subject: ela
items.title: Prefixes, suffixes, and homophones
items.summary: Prefixes like un- and re- and suffixes like -ful change meaning. Homophones sound alike but are spelled differently.

items.subject: ela
items.title: Discussion and presenting
items.summary: Come prepared, ask questions, stay on topic, and report on a topic with facts and a clear, strong voice.

items.subject: ela
items.title: English learners reading nonfiction
items.summary: Use pictures, headings, and a word list to understand a true book. Retell the key ideas with new English words.

items.subject: ela
items.title: Prefix words
items.summary: A prefix at the start changes the meaning of the word.

items.subject: ela
items.title: Suffix words
items.summary: Suffixes like -ful, -ly, -ness, and -er go on the end of a word.

items.subject: ela
items.title: Homophones
items.summary: These words sound the same but have different spellings and meanings.

items.subject: ela
items.title: Words about thinking
items.summary: These words help you talk about reading and learning.

items.subject: ela
items.title: Words that describe character
items.summary: Use these to tell what a character is like.

items.subject: ela
items.title: Theme and summarizing
items.summary: Find the theme, the big idea of a story, and write a short summary that includes the key events.

items.subject: ela
items.title: Quoting the text and inferring
items.summary: Say what a text says directly, and what you can infer from clues, by quoting exact words as proof.

items.subject: ela
items.title: First-person and third-person narration
items.summary: Compare stories told by a character (I) with ones told by an outside narrator (he, she, they).

items.subject: ela
items.title: How nonfiction is organized
items.summary: Authors organize facts by time order, cause and effect, comparison, or problem and solution.

items.subject: ela
items.title: Opinion writing with reasons
items.summary: State an opinion, support it with reasons and facts, and link ideas with words like for instance and in addition.

items.subject: ela
items.title: Informative writing and research
items.summary: Write about a topic with facts, definitions, and details, and use a few sources to build your knowledge.

items.subject: ela
items.title: Narrative writing
items.summary: Tell a story with a problem, vivid details, dialogue, and a satisfying ending.

items.subject: ela
items.title: Figurative language
items.summary: Similes compare using like or as, metaphors say one thing is another, and idioms like piece of cake mean something different from the words.

items.subject: ela
items.title: Greek and Latin roots
items.summary: Roots carry meaning: tele means far and scope means see, so a telescope helps you see far.

items.subject: ela
items.title: Sentences: fragments, run-ons, and punctuation
items.summary: Fix fragments and run-ons, use commas in lists and before quotes, and capitalize titles and names.

items.subject: ela
items.title: Relative pronouns and prepositions
items.summary: Words like who, which, and that join ideas. Prepositional phrases like under the bridge tell where or when.

items.subject: ela
items.title: Presenting with evidence
items.summary: Report on a topic in an organized way, speak clearly, and respond to questions with details.

items.subject: ela
items.title: English learners and academic language
items.summary: Practice words like because and therefore to explain your thinking in speaking and writing.

items.subject: ela
items.title: Greek and Latin root words
items.summary: Learn the roots and you can spell and understand many long words.

items.subject: ela
items.title: -tion and -sion words
items.summary: The endings -tion and -sion both say shun.

items.subject: ela
items.title: Commonly confused words
items.summary: These pairs trip up writers, so check the meaning before you pick a spelling.

items.subject: ela
items.title: Academic words
items.summary: Words you will meet in every subject.

items.subject: ela
items.title: Words for strong writing
items.summary: Swap ordinary words for stronger ones: tired becomes exhausted.

items.subject: ela
items.title: Quoting accurately and drawing inferences
items.summary: Quote the exact words from a story to explain what it says and what you infer.

items.subject: ela
items.title: Theme and summary
items.summary: Show how characters respond to challenges, and tell how a theme grows through the story.

items.subject: ela
items.title: Comparing stories and points of view
items.summary: Compare how narrators and characters see events, and how stories of the same kind treat similar themes.

items.subject: ela
items.title: Explaining ideas and relationships
items.summary: Tell how events, ideas, or steps in a nonfiction text connect, with cause and effect or compare and contrast.

items.subject: ela
items.title: Comparing multiple accounts
items.summary: Read two accounts of the same event and notice what each one stresses and where they agree.

items.subject: ela
items.title: Opinion writing with evidence
items.summary: Introduce a topic, state your opinion, support it with logical reasons and facts, and end with a conclusion.

items.subject: ela
items.title: Informative writing and research
items.summary: Organize ideas in paragraphs, use text features, quote or paraphrase sources, and list them.

items.subject: ela
items.title: Narrative writing
items.summary: Use dialogue, description, pacing, and transition words to tell an event sequence.

items.subject: ela
items.title: Conjunctions, interjections, and perfect tenses
items.summary: Conjunctions join ideas, interjections show feeling, and perfect tenses like I have walked show timing.

items.subject: ela
items.title: Commas and punctuation
items.summary: Use commas in a series, to set off introductions, and in direct address. Underline or italicize titles.

items.subject: ela
items.title: Word meaning: Greek and Latin affixes
items.summary: Use roots and affixes to figure out new words, and use context and a dictionary to check.

items.subject: ela
items.title: Figurative language
items.summary: Metaphors, similes, idioms, adages, and proverbs add color. A proverb like a stitch in time saves nine gives advice.

items.subject: ela
items.title: Collaborative discussions
items.summary: Prepare, follow agreed rules, ask questions, and add your thoughts to build on what others say.

items.subject: ela
items.title: English learners expanding language
items.summary: Use more precise verbs and connecting words to explain, compare, and persuade in English.

items.subject: ela
items.title: -able and -ible words
items.summary: Both endings mean able to be. Usually -able is added to complete words.

items.subject: ela
items.title: -ance and -ence words
items.summary: These endings turn words into nouns, and they are easy to mix up.

items.subject: ela
items.title: Tricky words
items.summary: Silent letters and unusual patterns make these tricky to spell.

items.subject: ela
items.title: Academic words
items.summary: Use these to talk about reading, science, and social studies.

items.subject: ela
items.title: Words for strong feelings and actions
items.summary: Choose just the right word for a character or a scene.

items.subject: ela
items.title: Citing evidence and theme
items.summary: Support your ideas with strong textual evidence, and show how a theme develops through details.

items.subject: ela
items.title: Central idea and author's point of view
items.summary: Find the central idea of a text, and tell how the author's word choices show their point of view.

items.subject: ela
items.title: Argument writing
items.summary: State a clear claim, give logical reasons with relevant evidence, and use credible sources.

items.subject: ela
items.title: Informative writing and research
items.summary: Write to explain a topic using facts, definitions, and examples, with organized paragraphs and transitions.

items.subject: ela
items.title: Pronouns and sentence variety
items.summary: Use pronouns in the right case and mix sentence lengths so your writing flows.

items.subject: ela
items.title: Word roots and context
items.summary: Use Greek and Latin roots, context clues, and a dictionary to find the meaning of tough words.

items.subject: ela
items.title: Presenting claims
items.summary: Organize a presentation with eye contact, clear volume, and evidence, and think about the speaker's reasons.

items.subject: ela
items.title: English learners and academic writing
items.summary: Use sentence frames and connecting words to write arguments and explanations in English.

items.subject: ela
items.title: Greek and Latin root words
items.summary: Use roots to unlock spelling and meaning.

items.subject: ela
items.title: Words often misspelled
items.summary: Study these tricky words and note the part that gets mixed up.

items.subject: ela
items.title: Academic words for grade 6
items.summary: Words you will use every day in class.

items.subject: ela
items.title: Theme and character development
items.summary: Trace how a theme develops across a story and how characters change because of events.

items.subject: ela
items.title: Analyzing arguments
items.summary: Tell what claim an author makes and whether the reasons and evidence are relevant and enough.

items.subject: ela
items.title: Argument writing with counterclaims
items.summary: Support a claim with reasons and evidence, and respond to opposing views in a fair, respectful way.

items.subject: ela
items.title: Narrative writing
items.summary: Use pacing, description, and reflection to tell a real or imagined experience.

items.subject: ela
items.title: Phrases, clauses, and sentence types
items.summary: Understand simple, compound, complex, and compound-complex sentences, and use commas correctly.

items.subject: ela
items.title: Word choice and figurative language
items.summary: Consider denotation, connotation, and figurative meaning. Cool and chilly can feel different.

items.subject: ela
items.title: Discussion and evaluating speakers
items.summary: Come prepared, build on others' ideas, and judge whether a speaker's reasoning is sound.

items.subject: ela
items.title: English learners and extended discourse
items.summary: Practice longer, structured spoken and written responses using academic language.

items.subject: ela
items.title: Words often misspelled
items.summary: These words are famous for tripping people up.

items.subject: ela
items.title: Academic words for grade 7
items.summary: Use these precise words in discussions and writing.

items.subject: ela
items.title: Analyzing structure and theme
items.summary: Analyze how a text is built, including how a theme or character grows and how stories draw on myths and older works.

items.subject: ela
items.title: Evaluating arguments and evidence
items.summary: Judge whether an argument is sound, and spot faulty reasoning or claims without enough evidence.

items.subject: ela
items.title: Argument and informative writing
items.summary: Write arguments with clear claims, counterclaims, and organized evidence, and informative texts that develop a topic in depth.

items.subject: ela
items.title: Narrative techniques
items.summary: Use dialogue, pacing, description, and reflection to build a story that hooks readers.

items.subject: ela
items.title: Verbals and voice
items.summary: Understand gerunds, participles, and infinitives, and choose between active and passive voice on purpose.

items.subject: ela
items.title: Verb mood and punctuation
items.summary: Use indicative, imperative, interrogative, conditional, and subjunctive moods, and punctuate with ellipses and dashes.

items.subject: ela
items.title: Delivering a presentation
items.summary: Present claims in a focused order, with evidence and clear speech, and weigh the speaker's reasoning.

items.subject: ela
items.title: English learners and academic English
items.summary: Use varied sentence types and precise vocabulary to express complex ideas in English.

items.subject: ela
items.title: Latin and Greek root words
items.summary: Roots help you spell and define advanced words.

items.subject: ela
items.title: Academic words for grade 8
items.summary: Words for analyzing texts and arguments.
